logic: The SPAYD text of a payment QR that the browser composes with spayd() (features/donations/spayd.ts) from what GET /api/donations/payment-details serves and the payment's amount in hellers, variable symbol and purpose (DONATION when left out), or its refusal as the fields it refuses. details names the case of payment/details.json whose answer the browser holds, so the recipient cases chain from the name the backend writes as SPAYD text; servedDetails is an answer the backend never gives (PaymentDetails refuses it at startup), which spayd() refuses rather than send. spayd() has no text rules of its own: it writes ACC, AM (crowns with two decimals, 1 heller to 9 999 999,99 Kč, the 10 characters SPAYD allows), CC, X-VS (only with a symbol, 1 to 10 digits; an account verification needs one), RN (left out when empty) and MSG (the purpose's message) as they come, and refuses details that are not SPAYD text (upper-case 0-9 A-Z $ + - . / : with single spaces, at most 35 characters for RN, 1 to 60 for both messages, whichever purpose is asked), a currency that is not three capital letters, and an account whose IBAN is not the IBAN of its Czech account number (payment/account.json, the pairing BankAccount enforces at startup), so the whole text stays in the QR alphanumeric set, no value can carry the separator * and the QR pays the account number people read. The donation form's own limits (whole crowns from 1 to 1 000 000 Kč) are the payment panel's, outside these cases. Only the browser runs the cases (spayd.spec.ts); the backend's DonationPurposeSharedCasesTest reads the account-verification cases and checks that the import recognises their message at the verification amount. qr/payment.json encodes each text into its QR symbol under the same case name
